concepts.def: There is one God; opening words of Guru Granth Sahib; foundational Sikh monotheism.
From Guru Nanak (1469-1539) to Guru Gobind Singh (1666-1708); each appointed successor; Adi Granth final Guru.
Sikh scripture treated as living Guru since 1708; 1430 pages of hymns by Sikh Gurus and Hindu/Muslim saints.
Khalsa Sikh symbols: Kesh (uncut hair), Kara (steel bracelet), Kanga (comb), Kachera (shorts), Kirpan (sword).
Community of initiated Sikhs founded by Guru Gobind Singh at Vaisakhi; Five Beloved Ones (Panj Piare).
Selfless service; threefold: tan (physical), man (mental), dhan (material); central to Sikh ethics; langar example.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Sikhism Option — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Sikhism Option brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Sikhism Option.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

free_texts.hint: Started by Guru Nanak; open to all.
